trap-negation-contrast.notes: STANDING-TRAP FINDING, report only, never fix math inline: the Rogers-form constraints are written e_3 = e_2/e_1, e_4 = (1 - e_2^{-1})/(1 - e_1^{-1}), e_5 = (1 - e_2)/(1 - e_1). Tested numerically at mpmath dps=30 with x = 0.3+0.7i, y = -0.4+1.3i: the standard five-term relation D(x) - D(y) + D(y/x) - D((1-x^{-1})/(1-y^{-1})) + D((1-x)/(1-y)) evaluates to EXACTLY 0.0, while the block's orientation (e_4, e_5 inverted) evaluates to 1.979625777. Note e_3 = e_2/e_1 DOES match the standard form under the identification (x, y) = (e_1, e_2), so no relabelling of x and y rescues e_4 and e_5 - with e_1 = y the e_3 constraint breaks instead. Since D(1/z) = -D(z), the inversion is not a harmless convention: it flips two of the five signs. Proposed fix: e_4 = (1 - e_1^{-1})/(1 - e_2^{-1}) and e_5 = (1 - e_1)/(1 - e_2), or state explicitly the sign convention under which the given orientation closes.
